previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and gastroparesis was admitted for acute on chronic abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and uncontrolled hyperglycemia. She presented with a blood glucose of 456 and elevated liver enzymes but no severe acidosis. Her symptoms were attributed to poor glycemic control and exacerbation of gastroparesis, possibly influenced by dietary indiscretion. She was managed with insulin regimen adjustments—increasing glargine to 12 units in the morning and 15 at night, and setting mealtime humalog to 5 units before each meal. She continued treatment for MSSA bacteremia with cefazolin and vancomycin locks, and for Clostridium difficile with metronidazole. An ultrasound showed gallbladder wall thickening without acute cholecystitis, and a right upper extremity ultrasound confirmed a patent fistula with no abscess despite localized tenderness. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics, adhere to a low-fat, small-meal diet, monitor blood glucose, and follow up with endocrinology and gastroenterology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with T1DM, ESRD, HTN, and multiple recent admissions for 
gastroparesis who presented with abdominal pain, nausea and 
vomiting.

# Gastroparesis: Patient presented with abdominal pain, nausea 
and vomiting similar to her prior presentations of 
gastroparesis. Due to her elevated white count to 17k on ___, 
a leukocytosis workup was performed which was negative (see 
below). She was treated supportively with IV and PO pain 
medications, as well as IV and PO anti-nausea medications. Her 
symptoms had largely resolved by ___ after she was dialyzed.

# Hypoglycemia: Endorsed compliance with her home insulin 
regimen with the exception of not taking her mealtime insulin 
for the 24 hours prior to admission because she had not been 
eating (due to nausea). The ___ hospital course was 
complicated by recurrent hypoglycemia (despite a significant 
reduction in her home insulin regimen while inpatient) requiring 
a ___ NS drip for approximately 24 hours. She had 
hemodialysis on ___ and ___ prior to admission (a disruption 
of her usual ___ HD schedule due to the holidays) and it 
is possible that her hypoglycemia was due to insulin stacking in 
the setting of a shorter duration of HD on those days. Her 
hypoglycemia resolved after she was dialyzed in hospital on 
___. ___ was consulted and made daily adjustments to her 
insulin regimen during her stay.

# Ascites / Leukocytosis / Abdominal pain: On admission, pt had 
a WBC of 17.7k. Blood cultures were NGTD after 4 days. While a 
CXR revealed an subtle opacity that could resemble PNA, she had 
no respiratory symptoms and was afebrile so this was not 
treated. She had a RUQ ultrasound which revealed moderate 
ascites, patent portal vein and patent visualized portions of 
the hepatic veins without any evidence of hepatic congestion. 
The liver was normal in appearance and the spleen was not 
enlarged. She had a diagnostic paracentesis performed on ___, 
with ascitic fluid analysis consistent with portal hypertension 
(SAAG > 1.1), 132 WBCs (5% polys). Ascitic fluid culture grew 
Bacillus species after several days which was felt to be a 
contaminant. She tested negative for Hepatitis A and B on 
___, and Hepatitis C on ___. She also had a CT 
Abdomen/Pelvis which did not reveal any findings to explain her 
abdominal pain. The medical team felt that her adominal pain was 
most consistent with her chronic gastroparetic pain combined 
with an overlying psychosomatic layer and, as a result, felt 
that it was appropriate to discharge the patient home. We 
recommend obtaining an MRI Liver as an outpatient to evaluate 
for regenerative nodular hyperplasia as a possible cause of her 
apparent portal hypertension and ascites, however there is no 
reason to believe that this would be contributing to her 
abdominal pain.

====== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ======

# Ascites: Recommend obtaining a Liver MRI to evaluate for 
regenerative nodular hyperplasia as the cause of her apparent 
portal hypertension and ascites.

# Gastroparesis: Patient was scheduled to follow up in the GI
